doc.title: Charles Lloyd — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The Monterey set: Booker's Garden, a Lady Day requiem and the church
summary: Lloyd describes how he played to five thousand people, moving from Moses to a requiem for Lady Day, Booker's Garden, the Flower and Pentecostal music.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: There was five thousand people out there, I wasn't... In an arena you’re supposed to scream.
And the Orchestra was so. And Dorothy asked Jason "How was it?" he said "It was off the hook!" [laughs]

And Eric said "When this orchestra plays it's a magical thing." But what I was getting at.. now be quiet... I went into, I went over some Moses and stuff, and then I went into a requiem I wrote for Lady Day, and then I went into the Flower... No, I went into Booker's Garden.
I played some for Booker and then I went into the Flower, and then I went into the church.
And then I went into the Pentecostal stuff, and the boys were screaming and yelling and stuff you know, and the people, they kinda lost it. [Laughs]
